issues.body: `classify_pre_session` checks only `method` and non-null `id`, while `route_post` mints whenever `handle_message` returns any response. For example, `{"jsonrpc":5,"id":1,"method":"initialize","params":{}}` is classified as `Handshake`; JSON-RPC request deserialization then returns an error response because `jsonrpc` is not a string, but the transport still creates a session and attaches `mcp-session-id`. The comment and public documentation promise that only a successful initialize mints a session.
issues.fix_hint: Mint only when dispatch reports a successful initialize result, preferably via a typed dispatch outcome rather than inspecting serialized JSON. Add a regression test using an initialize-shaped request that produces a JSON-RPC error; assert there is no session header, `session_count() == 0`, and no later request can use a would-be session.
issues.title: Failed initialize requests still mint live sessions

issues.body: `read_request` retains every header, but `lookup("content-length")` selects only the first occurrence. A request with conflicting Content-Length fields is therefore framed according to the first value even though an intermediary may reject, combine, or select another value. Closing the backend connection does not eliminate the proxy/backend framing disagreement, and this contradicts the parser's stated refuse-rather-than-guess invariant.
issues.fix_hint: Collect all Content-Length occurrences before reading the body and reject duplicates (or accept only when every strictly parsed value is identical). Reject comma-joined and malformed forms. Add focused parser tests for conflicting duplicates and duplicate-equal fields to pin the policy.
issues.title: Conflicting duplicate Content-Length headers are still accepted

verdict.summary: Round 5 is stagnant: both round-4 major findings remain in the PR head. Pre-session classification still admits an initialize-shaped object without validating the JSON-RPC fields that the dispatcher deserializes, and route_post still mints a session for any returned reply, including an error reply. The HTTP parser also still selects the first Content-Length occurrence and accepts duplicate/conflicting values, preserving a request-framing ambiguity. Neither load-bearing regression test requested in round 4 is present.
